events.title: Nguyen Huu Canh inspected Dong Nai
events.description: Commander Nguyen Huu Canh obeyed the orders of Lord Nguyen Phuc Chu to inspect the land of Dong Nai, establishing Gia Dinh Prefecture, which included Phuoc Long District (Tran Bien Garrison - present-day Dong Nai) and Tan Binh District (Phien Tran Garrison - Saigon). This was the milestone that birthed the Southern region onto the administrative map of Vietnam.

events.title: Establishment of the Binh Phuoc - Tan Trieu Party Cell
events.description: In Binh Phuoc Village (now in Tan Binh Commune), the first Communist Party Cell of Bien Hoa Province was established. This was the core leadership of the revolutionary movement in Bien Hoa during its infancy.

events.title: Seizing power in Bien Hoa
events.description: About 10,000 people from Chau Thanh and Long Thanh districts and factory workers gathered at Song Pho Square to attend a rally. Province Chief Nguyen Ba Thuoc was forced to hand over the official seal. The Provisional Revolutionary People's Committee of Bien Hoa Province made its debut to the public.

events.title: Establishment of War Zone D
events.description: War Zone D was established, encompassing the rugged mountainous and forested area north of the Dong Nai River (in Vinh Cuu, Dong Nai and Tan Uyen, Binh Duong). This was a legendary resistance base, the 'resistance capital' of the Southeast region.

events.title: The La Nga Ambush
events.description: Detachment 10 and Allied Force 17 organized an ambush against a French military convoy on National Route 20 (near La Nga Bridge). Our forces destroyed 59 vehicles and killed 150 enemy troops (including Colonel De Serigne and many high-ranking officers). This victory resonated across the country.

events.title: The Nha Xanh Attack (The first battle against the US)
events.description: Bien Hoa sappers boldly attacked Nha Xanh (the headquarters of the US Military Assistance Advisory Group - MAAG) in Bien Hoa, killing 2 US advisors. This is considered the first battle to eliminate US soldiers on the Southern battlefield, signaling the failure of the 'Americanization' of the war policy.

events.title: Attack on Bien Hoa Airbase
events.description: The Regional Artillery Group (U80) secretly launched a heavy bombardment on Bien Hoa Airbase - a strategic US airbase. The attack destroyed and damaged 59 aircraft, killed and wounded nearly 300 enemy troops, shocking the Pentagon.

events.title: Tet Offensive (Bien Hoa - Long Binh Front)
events.description: The Liberation Army simultaneously attacked key targets: Bien Hoa Airbase, Long Binh Depot, the III Corps Headquarters... At Long Binh Depot, our sappers destroyed the largest US ammunition depot in the South, causing massive explosions and fires for several days.

events.title: Xuan Loc Victory (Smashing the 'Steel Gate')
events.description: After 12 days and nights of fierce fighting (April 9 - April 21), the regular 4th Corps smashed the enemy's most fortified defense line at Xuan Loc - Long Khanh (the 'Steel Gate' protecting Saigon from the East). This victory shook the Saigon regime, opening the way for the main army to advance to the Independence Palace.

events.title: Liberation of Bien Hoa
events.description: On the morning of April 30, the 2nd Corps and local forces attacked and completely liberated Bien Hoa City, capturing Bien Hoa Airbase and the puppet III Corps Headquarters, smashing the final defense line at the northeastern gateway to Saigon.

events.title: Cat Tien National Park recognized by UNESCO
events.description: UNESCO recognized Cat Tien National Park as a World Biosphere Reserve (the 411th). This is one of the most important nature reserves in Vietnam with rich flora and fauna, where the last population of the one-horned Javan rhinoceros was once discovered.
